title: Naming: PartCollection/reassemble (uu-multi) vs Assembler/finish (yenc-multi) for same concept
description:
## Finding

uuencoding-multi and yencoding-multi both implement multi-part binary reassembly, but use entirely different names for every public concept:

| Concept | uuencoding-multi | yencoding-multi |
|---|---|---|
| Accumulator type | PartCollection | Assembler |
| Terminal operation | reassemble(&coll) | assembler.finish() |
| Error type | MultiUuError | AssemblyError |
| Result type | ReassembledFile | Vec<u8> |
| Part input | PartEntry | DecodedPart |

## Impact

A caller that switches from UUencoding to yEnc, or handles both formats, must learn two completely parallel vocabularies for the same concept. A maintainer adding a third encoding format has no canonical naming pattern to extend. The divergence is not justified by any protocol difference — both formats accumulate decoded parts and assemble them into a complete file.
close_reason: Naming reflects different domain patterns. Renaming would be breaking. Same root as MIME-8zt.8.
